Does my voice leave my PC?+

Speech recognition and text cleanup run locally. Saydraft has no cloud transcription, telemetry, or account. Model downloads happen only when you start them during setup. Optional update checks are off by default and request public release information from GitHub without your audio or text.

Do I need the internet to get started?+

Yes, once: choose the recommended models, review their sizes and licenses, and start the setup download. You can pause and resume. Later launches reuse the installed models offline.

Which languages can I dictate in?+

Thai, Mandarin Chinese, Korean, Japanese, Hindi, Urdu, Vietnamese, Filipino / Tagalog, Tamil, Telugu, Persian, Indonesian, Malay, Bengali and Arabic use the optional shared All languages model. Spanish, French, German and Portuguese, including Brazilian Portuguese, are covered by the default Parakeet v3 model and All languages. There are no separate language packs. Choosing a language starts no download.

Do I need a powerful graphics card?+

Speech recognition can run on the CPU. Hardware and model choice affect speed; optional AI cleanup requires more resources. The performance check helps choose a suitable setup, including rules-only cleanup.

Where can I use it?+

Saydraft inserts text at the cursor in editable Windows apps. Password fields are excluded. Some protected or elevated apps need extra care; start with an ordinary text editor.

Can I change how my words are cleaned up?+

Choose a tone and cleanup intensity for each app group, add names to your dictionary, and create spoken snippets. Raw mode preserves your transcript without prose cleanup.

Is it free?+

Saydraft is free and open source under the MIT license. Speech and cleanup models have their own licenses, shown before download and listed in the project credits.

Is this page listening to me?+

No. The example is a canned simulation. This website does not request microphone access, upload audio, or use tracking analytics.

Does my voice leave my PC?+

Speech recognition and text cleanup run locally. Saydraft has no cloud transcription, telemetry, or account. Model downloads happen only when you start them during setup. Optional update checks are off by default and request public release information from GitHub without your audio or text.

Do I need the internet to get started?+

Yes, once: choose the recommended models, review their sizes and licenses, and start the setup download. You can pause and resume. Later launches reuse the installed models offline.

Which languages can I dictate in?+

Thai, Mandarin Chinese, Korean, Japanese, Hindi, Urdu, Vietnamese, Filipino / Tagalog, Tamil, Telugu, Persian, Indonesian, Malay, Bengali and Arabic use the optional shared All languages model. Spanish, French, German and Portuguese, including Brazilian Portuguese, are covered by the default Parakeet v3 model and All languages. There are no separate language packs. Choosing a language starts no download.

Do I need a powerful graphics card?+

Speech recognition can run on the CPU. Hardware and model choice affect speed; optional AI cleanup requires more resources. The performance check helps choose a suitable setup, including rules-only cleanup.

Where can I use it?+

Saydraft inserts text at the cursor in editable Windows apps. Password fields are excluded. Some protected or elevated apps need extra care; start with an ordinary text editor.

Can I change how my words are cleaned up?+

Choose a tone and cleanup intensity for each app group, add names to your dictionary, and create spoken snippets. Raw mode preserves your transcript without prose cleanup.

Is it free?+

Saydraft is free and open source under the MIT license. Speech and cleanup models have their own licenses, shown before download and listed in the project credits.

Is this page listening to me?+

No. The example is a canned simulation. This website does not request microphone access, upload audio, or use tracking analytics.
